title: brewers demolish reds 20 0 wrap up postseason berth  flm 2026 09 12
text:
September 12 - Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in six runs, and Dustin May tossed six innings of two-hit ball as the Milwaukee Brewers routed ​the visiting Cincinnati Reds 20-0 on Friday night to clinch their eighth postseason ‌berth in nine seasons.
The Brewers fell short of the biggest shutout in modern major league history, a record they tied on Aug. 18 by trouncing the Seattle Mariners 22-0.
May (7-9), acquired at the trade deadline from the ​St. Louis Cardinals, allowed singles in the first and fourth innings, both to Sal ​Stewart. May struck out six and walked one in an 84-pitch outing ⁠to improve to 2-2 with Milwaukee.
Rookie Garrett Stallings pitched the final three innings for his ​first save.
Mitchell's 10th homer of the year and first career grand slam capped an eight-run fifth ​that put the Brewers up 17-0. Brice Turang (3-for-3, four RBIs) and Jake Bauers homered during a six-run second when Milwaukee went in front 8-0.
Contreras belted a three-run homer in the eighth off catcher Jose Trevino, who ​pitched the final two innings for the Reds.
Milwaukee (92-56) pounded out a season-high 23 hits and ​won its fourth straight to maintain a 10-game lead in the National League Central over the Chicago Cubs (82-66), ‌who ⁠won earlier Friday. The Brewers, bidding for their fourth consecutive division title, are 1 1/2 games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best overall record in the majors.
The Brewers jumped on Andrew Abbott (6-11) for two runs in the first and six in the second, ending his ​outing after he allowed ​nine hits on ⁠43 pitches. Cincinnati (69-78) has lost four straight.
Contreras (sacrifice fly) and Andrew Vaughn (double) had the RBIs in the first inning.
Cooper Pratt and Mitchell opened the second ​with consecutive singles. Jackson Chourio's one-out ground-rule double scored Pratt to ​make it 3-0. ⁠Turang then lined a 1-2 pitch 382 feet to right-center for a three-run homer. Vaughn singled with two outs, and Bauers followed with a 412-foot shot to center.
Milwaukee added a run the ⁠fourth when ​Turang drew a leadoff walk and scored when Bauers' ​two-out single was misplayed for an outfield error.
Rookie Luis Lara kept the Reds off the board in the fifth with ​a sensational leaping grab above the right field wall on Eugenio Suarez's potential homer.
--Field Level Media
